 NA Counter-Strike legend Rambo nominated for HLTV Hall of Fame
 An old legend joins two other Americans on the short list. 
 HLTV has released the latest slate of players up for potential induction into the HLTV Hall of Fame, with American Counter-Strike legend Ronald "Rambo" Kim up for consideration as part of the Class of 2026. Rambo joins two other American names up for induction, with Daniel "fRoD" Montaner and Kyle "KSharp" Miller also appearing on the ballet, both for the third time in a row.
 Also read: Stake announces Swedish Pulse LAN series will continue in 2027 with six LANs 
 Rambo was one of the early stars of the North American Counter-Strike scene, with the 42-year-old player competing in some of the games first big LAN events including the game's second S-tier event, as defined by Liquipedia, Babbage's CPL 2000. Rambo's accolades include winning two CPL events in 2001 and 2002 with X3 Blue and 3D, and two World Cyber Games medals in 2004 and 2005.
 Later Rambo would go on to compete in Counter-Strike: Source 's ill-fated Championship Gaming Series with LA compLexity, winning a number of standalone events before eventually hanging up the mouse as a player in 2010. After a number of years away from the game, Rambo later returned in Counter-Strike: Global Offensive as a coach for Korean team MVP PK and later compLexity and Cloud9.
